name: Serena
outcome_statement: As of 2026-11-14: meets C3, C4, C6, C7, C9, C10; partly meets C1, C2, C5, C8.

findings.title: Source and release provenance
findings.finding: The PyPI record for serena-agent 2.1.0 links the repository. PyPI holds no provenance attestation for the release (the integrity record returned HTTP 404).

findings.title: Published security policy
findings.finding: GitHub's security-policy page for the repository says "No security policy detected"; the same page offers private vulnerability reporting ("Report a vulnerability").

findings.title: Maintenance status
findings.finding: The repository is not archived and the package is not marked deprecated. Latest release 2.1.0 is dated 2026-10-19; the newest commit on `main` is dated 2026-11-14; GitHub reports the last push on 2026-11-14.

findings.title: Published advisories
findings.finding: 3 advisories are published in the repository's advisory list; each names a patched version at or below the latest release (2.1.0). Most recent: GHSA-pp6p-xvxf-8hhx (high, published 2026-10-14, patched in 2.0.0).

findings.title: Documented scope controls
findings.finding: A shell-command tool and file-editing tools are documented; the README says such tools are typically disabled by default inside agentic harnesses, and the security documentation recommends restricting the allowed tools through configuration. Quoted: “**`execute_shell_command`** – run shell commands (e.g. builds, tests, linters)”; “When Serena is used inside an agentic harness such as Claude Code or Codex, these tools are typically disabled by default,”; “restrict the set of allowed tools via the configuration”.

findings.title: Credential handling in the documented setup
findings.finding: The documented setup takes no credential. Searched `README.md` for: API_KEY, _TOKEN\b, password.

findings.title: Telemetry and outbound data, as documented
findings.finding: The README contains no reference to telemetry or usage collection, and the documented function contacts only the service the user configures. Searched `README.md` for: telemetry, usage statistics, usage stats, we collect, data collection, opt-out, posthog.

findings.title: Dependency management files
findings.finding: A lockfile (`uv.lock`) is committed. No Dependabot or Renovate configuration file exists at the paths listed in the methodology.

findings.title: Documentation of untrusted-content risk
findings.finding: The project's security documentation says the contents of a repository can influence the model, documents a project-trust setting, and recommends sandboxing for repositories that are not trusted. Quoted: “the repository’s contents can influence the LLM”; “If a repository is not trustworthy, sandboxing is the answer, not the trust configuration.”.

findings.title: Currency of the declared MCP library
findings.finding: Declared MCP library: mcp==2.2.0. Lower-bound version 2.2.0 of mcp (PyPI) was published on 2026-09-07, within the 12 months before 2026-11-14.

advisories.summary: Remote Code Execution via insecure pickle deserialization of LSP symbol cache (malicious repository → RCE on project activation)
Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in mode/context prompt rendering → RCE on project activation, bypassing `trusted_project_path_patterns`
Unauthenticated Flask dashboard on fixed port enables DNS rebinding → memory poisoning → RCE
